methodology: One explicitly imported account; six real upstream requests, no tool execution, no hidden retries, one sample per variant.

First request actually truncated tool JSON with upstream MAX_TOKENS. All subsequent cases reuse its literal outgoing body, including conversation ID and max_tokens=4096, and change only current user content, if any.
Old first instruction appends the production 20-line/4000-character snapshot. Old second appends both first and second (10-line/2000-character) snapshots to reproduce cumulative instruction text.

New first uses production tool_recovery_request. New second applies it twice. These are alternative prompt branches, not one sequential production recovery flow. Second-stage variants test accumulated prompt text only; the first new variant returned explanatory text and would not trigger another automatic production recovery.
Unchanged control resends the literal baseline body with identical SHA-256. Failed prefixes are never added to history or executed.

Actual request body and recovery field preservation checked after endpoint and account shaping, immediately before execute. Direct raw frames decoded; HTTP 200 is not counted as complete task fulfillment.
Each call limited to 90 seconds and 1 MiB response. No credentials, profile, auth headers or account identifiers recorded.
policySource: 20/10 lines and 4000/2000 characters were introduced by local commit 5b15337 (2026-11-04), with no accompanying official reference or reproducible live evidence for those exact numbers.
findings: Original 550-line/30250-character task actually truncated at max_tokens=4096. The unchanged request also truncated.
Old first instruction returned complete JSON for only the first 10 lines/550 characters; old second returned only first 5 lines/275 characters. Neither exact-matched the requested complete payload.
New recovery instructions returned explanatory text with no tool calls in both accumulated-instruction variants; no complete task result was produced.
This low-budget experiment supports neither an optimal size threshold nor a general recovery success rate. Old hints produced syntactically complete partial work, not full task recovery.
Previous independent output-budget evidence shows this task completed with max_tokens=16384 and no size prompt; this experiment does not increase caller native budget during recovery.
decision: Remove fixed numeric line/character caps, forced one-tool count, skeleton-first and tool-switch bans from recovery prompt. Preserve task/content/scope and native controls; report prior truncation and request complete regenerated JSON, with an explanation if it cannot fit. No replacement size cap, budget inflation, response schema enforcement or new retry introduced.
limits: Single account/model/endpoint/region/date and fixed branch order. One sample per variant. No exact output token usage reported. Does not prove numeric limits are never useful, or new instructions guarantee success. Second-stage variants test cumulative instructions rather than an actual second production retry following another truncated response.
